items.title: Sub-Gaussian variables and vectors, and sub-exponential variables
items.statement:
Use the real random variable convention of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]] and the expectation convention of [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]]. A real random variable $X$ is **centered** when it is integrable and $\mathbb E X=0$. A vector random element $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_d)$ in $\mathbb R^d$, for an integer $d\ge1$, is centered when each coordinate is integrable and $\mathbb E Z_j=0$. For $u,z\in\mathbb R^d$, write $\langle u,z\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^d u_jz_j$ and $\|u\|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^d u_j^2)^{1/2}$, using the Euclidean convention in [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]].

For $\sigma^2\ge0$, a centered real random variable $X$ is **sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2$** if
$$\mathbb E e^{\lambda X}\le e^{\lambda^2\sigma^2/2}\qquad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R.$$
A centered vector random element $Z\in\mathbb R^d$ is **sub-Gaussian with proxy $\sigma^2$** if
$$\mathbb E e^{\lambda\langle u,Z\rangle}\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2\|u\|_2^2/2}\qquad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^d\text{ and }\lambda\in\mathbb R.$$

For $\nu^2\ge0$ and $b>0$, a centered real random variable $X$ is **sub-exponential with parameters $(\nu^2,b)$** if
$$\mathbb E e^{\lambda X}\le e^{\lambda^2\nu^2/2}\qquad\text{whenever }|\lambda|\le1/b.$$

The parameters $\sigma^2$ and $\nu^2$ are moment-generating-function upper-bound proxies; they are not asserted to equal the variance. The vector condition controls every one-dimensional projection and does not assert independence of coordinates.

items.title: Hoeffding inequality for independent bounded sums
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$ and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent integrable real random variables on one probability space. Suppose finite real numbers $a_i\le b_i$ satisfy $a_i\le X_i\le b_i$ almost surely for every $i$. Put $V=\sum_{i=1}^n(b_i-a_i)^2$ and $S=\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\mathbb E X_i)$. For every $t>0$, if $V>0$ then
$$\mathbb P(|S|\ge t)\le 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{2t^2}{V}\right),$$
and if $V=0$ then $\mathbb P(|S|\ge t)=0$. The two one-sided tails are each bounded by $\exp(-2t^2/V)$ when $V>0$.

items.title: Bernstein inequality for bounded independent sums
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent centered square-integrable real random variables. Suppose $b\ge0$ is finite and $|X_i|\le b$ almost surely for each $i$. Put $v=\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Var}(X_i)$. For $t>0$, if $v>0$ then
$$\mathbb P\left(\left|\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\right|\ge t\right)\le 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(v+bt/3)}\right),$$
and if $v=0$ then this probability is $0$.

items.title: Finite epsilon nets of the Euclidean sphere
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer and $0<\epsilon<1$. There is a finite set $\mathcal N\subseteq S^{d-1}$ such that every $u\in S^{d-1}$ has some $v\in\mathcal N$ with $\|u-v\|_2\le\epsilon$, and
$$|\mathcal N|\le(1+2/\epsilon)^d.$$
Here $S^{d-1}=\{u\in\mathbb R^d:\|u\|_2=1\}$ by [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]. Such a set is called an $\epsilon$-net of the sphere.

items.title: Doob differences inherit coordinate oscillation widths
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ be independent random elements with laws $\mu_i$ on measurable spaces $(S_i,\Sigma_i)$, and let $\mu=\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\mu_i$. Let $f:\prod_{i=1}^nS_i\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$. Suppose finite deterministic $c_i\ge0$ satisfy
$$|f(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},x_i,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_n)-f(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},x_i',x_{i+1},\ldots,x_n)|\le c_i$$
for every $i$, every fixed choice of the other coordinates, and every $x_i,x_i'\in S_i$. For each $i$, define $M_i$ by integrating $f$ over the unrevealed product coordinates, using the measurable finite versions given by Fubini; set $M_0=\int f\,d\mu$ and $M_n=f(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$. Put $\mathcal F_i=\sigma(Z_1,\ldots,Z_i)$ and $D_i=M_i-M_{i-1}$. Then $M_i$ is integrable and $\mathcal F_i$-measurable, and for every $A\in\mathcal F_{i-1}$,
$$\int_A D_i\,d\mathbb P=0.$$
Moreover, there are finite $\mathcal F_{i-1}$-measurable endpoints $A_i,B_i$ such that $A_i\le0\le B_i$, $A_i\le D_i\le B_i$ almost surely, and $B_i-A_i\le c_i$ almost surely. No choice axiom is used in this product-integral construction.

items.title: Sub-exponential concentration for independent sums
items.statement:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent centered real random variables, with $X_i$ sub-exponential with parameters $(\nu_i^2,b_i)$ as defined in [[def-subgaussian-variable-and-vector]], where $n\ge1$ and $b_i>0$. Put $v=\sum_{i=1}^n\nu_i^2$, $b=\max_{1\le i\le n}b_i$, and $S=\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$. For $t>0$, if $v>0$ then
$$\mathbb P(|S|\ge t)\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac12\min\!\left\{\frac{t^2}{v},\frac{t}{b}\right\}\right),$$
and if $v=0$ then $\mathbb P(|S|\ge t)=0$.

items.title: Finite sub-Gaussian maxima and epsilon-net reduction
items.statement:
Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be centered sub-Gaussian real random variables with a common proxy $\sigma^2\ge0$, where $m\ge1$. No independence is assumed. For $t>0$, if $\sigma^2>0$ then
$$\mathbb P\left(\max_{1\le j\le m}|Y_j|\ge t\right)\le2m\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),$$
and if $\sigma^2=0$ the probability is $0$.

Let $Z$ be a centered sub-Gaussian vector in $\mathbb R^d$ with proxy $\sigma^2$, where $d\ge1$. For $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\mathcal N$ be the sphere net supplied by [[lem-epsilon-net-of-unit-sphere-has-cardinality-bound]]. Then for $t>0$, if $\sigma^2>0$,
$$\mathbb P(\|Z\|_2\ge t)\le2(1+2/\epsilon)^d\exp\!\left(-\frac{(1-\epsilon)^2t^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),$$
and if $\sigma^2=0$ this probability is $0$. The deterministic reduction is $\|z\|_2\le(1-\epsilon)^{-1}\max_{u\in\mathcal N}|\langle u,z\rangle|$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^d$.

items.title: McDiarmid bounded-differences inequality
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $Z_i:(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\to(S_i,\Sigma_i)$ be independent random elements, meaning measurable maps ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]), with laws $\mu_i$ given by pushforward ([[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]). Put $\mu=\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\mu_i$ on the finite product sigma-algebra ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]). Let $f:\prod_{i=1}^nS_i\to\mathbb R$ be product-measurable with $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$. Suppose finite deterministic constants $c_i\ge0$ satisfy
$$|f(z_1,\ldots,z_i,\ldots,z_n)-f(z_1,\ldots,z_i',\ldots,z_n)|\le c_i$$
for every fixed setting of the other coordinates and every $z_i,z_i'$. The independent product-law theorem identifies the law of $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$ as $\mu$. Applying change of variables for expectation first to $|f|$ and then to $f$ makes $f(Z)$ integrable and gives $\mathbb E f(Z)=\int f\,d\mu$. Put $V=\sum_{i=1}^n c_i^2$. For $t>0$, if $V>0$ then
$$\mathbb P\bigl(f(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)-\mathbb E f(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\ge t\bigr)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{2t^2}{V}\right),$$
and if $V=0$ this probability is $0$. The same bound holds for the lower tail, so the two-sided probability is at most $2e^{-2t^2/V}$ when $V>0$.

items.title: A Rademacher sum
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$ and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent Rademacher variables, meaning $\mathbb P(X_i=1)=\mathbb P(X_i=-1)=1/2$, and put $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$. For every $t>0$,
$$\mathbb P(|S_n|\ge t)\le2e^{-t^2/(2n)}.$$

items.title: A Gaussian maximum without independence
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $\sigma>0$, let $G\sim N(0,1)$, and set $Z_j=\sigma G$ for every $1\le j\le m$, where $m\ge1$. These variables are perfectly dependent. For every $t>0$,
$$\mathbb P\left(\max_{1\le j\le m}|Z_j|\ge t\right)\le2m\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).$$

items.title: A sub-Gaussian vector norm bound
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $Z\in\mathbb R^d$ be a centered sub-Gaussian vector with proxy $\sigma^2>0$. Choosing $\epsilon=1/2$ in the net reduction gives, for every $t>0$,
$$\mathbb P(\|Z\|_2\ge t)\le2\cdot5^d e^{-t^2/(8\sigma^2)}.$$
If $\sigma^2=0$, the same probability is $0$.

items.title: Finite variance does not imply a sub-Gaussian tail
items.statement: Every centered real random variable with finite variance is sub-Gaussian with some finite proxy.
